newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count down six to 982 in week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count down six to 982 in week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 982 as of June 13, down six from the prior week and 209 above the year-ago total of 773, Baker Hughes Inc reported.
The number of rigs drilling on land fell by ten to 832, while rigs working offshore rose six to 126. The number of rigs active in inland waters dipped two to 24.
Among the individual states, the biggest changes occurred in Texas, which was down by 13. Louisiana was up by eight and Wyoming was up by two.
The Gulf of Mexico rig count rose six to 122.

A total of 393 rigs were exploring for crude oil, down nine from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas rose by five to 585, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects remained at four.
There were 208 rigs drilling directionally, 76 drilling horizontally and 698 drilling vertically.
In Canada, the number of working rigs rose by 50 to 336, versus 269 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
